newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon to award mail privatisation bids in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon to award mail privatisation bids in Nov.

text.p: Lebanon will announce in November the results of bids by international companies to take over postal services for 10 years at a cost of $30 million, a government official was quoted on Thursday as saying.
"The Ministry of Posts and Communications will grant the postal project in November to foreign companies," Omar Bendaq, director general of the ministry, told Beirut's an-Nahar daily.

France's Laposte, Canada's Canada Post and Elzaq-Baily of Italy and a consortium comprising Neposte of Holland and Jordan-based Aramex have submitted bids to take over the postal services for a 10-year period, government sources said in May.
Bendaq said the delay in awarding the bids was mainly due to government red tape and a 17-day Israeli blitz in April against Lebanon "which froze the studying of the bids for some time".
The services on offer were mail handling, express mail, facsimile service and philately.
If the tender is successful, the postal service which deteriorated during the 1975-90 civil war will be the first public utility to be privatised.
